question: What is the main goal of day and night hospital services?

options.A: To provide permanent housing for chronic psychiatric patients
options.B: To replace outpatient clinics entirely in rural areas
options.C: To isolate violent patients from their families permanently
options.D: To bridge the gap between full hospital admission and community life

explanation: Spot on! These services provide structured support while keeping patients connected to their families and everyday lives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h1)

question: How does a night hospital typically work for its clients?

options.A: Clients visit only for medication administration once a week at midnight
options.B: Clients sleep at the facility at night and work or attend school during the day
options.C: Clients receive therapy all night and sleep at home during the day
options.D: Clients stay locked in the ward 24 hours a day with weekend leave

explanation: You got it! Night hospitals provide a safe place to sleep overnight so clients can still go about their normal daytime routines. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which day hospital setup shares resources directly with a larger general or psychiatric hospital?
explanation: Well done! The integrated model is physically and administratively linked to a main hospital, sharing staff and facilities. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the main focus of a rehabilitation-focused day hospital?

options.A: Acute medical detoxification from alcohol and hard drugs
options.B: Providing emergency electroconvulsive therapy 24 hours a day
options.C: Strict physical containment of aggressive behavioral outbursts
options.D: Long-term skill building, socialization, and vocational readiness

explanation: Exactly! Rehabilitation centers help clients regain independence, learn practical skills, and get ready to return to work. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is needed for a patient to be admitted to a day hospital?

options.A: Medical stability and a safe home environment
options.B: Complete refusal of any psychiatric medication
options.D: Severe physical violence toward family members

explanation: Correct! Patients must be stable and have a safe place to go when they leave the facility for the day. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h3)

question: A patient with schizophrenia is leaving the inpatient ward. Which situation means they are NOT ready for a day hospital program?

options.A: They live alone in a supportive family compound
options.B: They attend church services every Sunday with relatives
options.C: They have active homicidal threats and a plan to harm a neighbor
options.D: They take their oral medications reliably every morning

explanation: Spot on! Active danger to others means the patient needs a secure inpatient ward rather than partial care. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why are group therapy sessions used so much in day hospitals?

options.A: They help build social skills and provide peer support
options.B: They reduce the number of staff members needed on duty
options.C: They are required by law for all nursing documentation
options.D: They eliminate the need for individual psychiatric evaluation

explanation: You're right! Groups give patients a safe space to practice talking with others and learn from shared experiences. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving out medications in a day hospital?

options.A: Monitoring clients for side effects like extrapyramidal symptoms
options.B: Hiding the medication from family members
options.C: Prescribing higher dosages when symptoms worsen
options.D: Allowing clients to choose whatever drug they prefer

explanation: Correct! Since clients spend a lot of time outside the hospital, nurses must watch closely for any unwanted drug reactions. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which group of professionals makes up the core mental health team?

options.C: Psychiatrists, nurses, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Hospital administrators, accountants, and security officers

explanation: Spot on! Good mental health care brings together medical, nursing, social, and daily living expertise. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why is helping clients connect with their community an important part of day and night hospital care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any ongoing medication
options.B: It reduces stigma and helps clients function within their social environment
options.C: It ensures patients never have to return to their families
options.D: It allows the hospital to discharge staff and save money

explanation: You got it! Keeping clients connected to their communities builds acceptance and supports long-term recovery. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h5)
